title: Quantized model deployment triggered eviction cascade and crash-loop; mitigation & long-term fixes
creator: Amelie Chen
description: A canary deployment of an INT4-quantized variant of 'gpt-lite-16k' caused a KV-cache eviction cascade and repeated worker restart loops in a dedicated pool. This ticket consolidates the incident follow-up, immediate mitigations applied, and owner-assigned action items for short- and long-term fixes.
timeline: 2025-11-08T02:14Z - Canary rollout started: 10% traffic to quantized variant via rollout policy 'canary-quant-2025-11-08'
2025-11-08T02:26Z - Increased 503 and OOM restarts detected in pool gpu-ded-3; auto-remediation started but thrash observed
2025-11-08T02:30Z - Oncall paged: latency spike and worker crash-loop in canary shard; initial rollback initiated for canary traffic
2025-11-08T02:37Z - Canary rollback completed; traffic restored to previous model variants; partial service degradation for <15 minutes
2025-11-08T03:10Z - Initial incident bridge: engineering, runtime, infra, and oncall leads convened
2025-11-08T10:00Z - Heap/profile dumps and kernel traces uploaded to GCS: gs://redwood-incident/2025-11-08/ENG-44211
2025-11-09T09:00Z - Root cause hypothesis refined after reproducer: aggressive KV cache growth + quantized kernel memory accounting bug -> eviction cascade
2025-11-11T14:30Z - Hotfix: conservative KV cache high-water mark applied to dedicated pools; emergency canary policy disabled until additional telemetry in place
2025-11-15T11:00Z - Nightly regression harness extended to include quantized footprint tracing and eviction simulation
2025-11-22T09:00Z - This ticket updated with owners for long-term fixes and observability work
impact_summary: Canary triggered a crash-loop affecting ~1 dedicated GPU pool. End-user API had transient 503s and increased tail latency for ~15 minutes. No data exfiltration. Several customers on Dedicated reported failed requests during the window.
root_cause: Two interacting issues: 1) quantized inference path altered memory accounting for per-request KV cache reservations (off-by-factor for int4 packed weights) causing misreported free memory; 2) autoscaler/concurrency logic allowed inflight requests to accumulate, forcing aggressive eviction that corrupted live KV entries under certain concurrency patterns. The bad memory accounting prevented proper backpressure, causing OOMs and restarts.
short_term_mitigations: Rollback canary and disable automated canary ramp for any quant-converter builds (done 2025-11-08)
Apply conservative KV cache HWM and smaller per-concurrency reservation on dedicated pools (hotfix deployed 2025-11-11)
Add immediate alerting for eviction rate > 20/min and worker restart loops (Pager duty alerted)
Temporarily pin runtime-1.27 to previous quant-converter binary for all production pools until validation passes
long_term_action_items: ENG-44211-A: Add deterministic unit tests for quantized memory accounting and packed-weight reservation (owner: Ravi) - due 2025-11-29
ENG-44211-B: Implement eviction-safe KV cache reconciliation routine to avoid entry corruption during concurrent evictions (owner: Priya Shah) - due 2025-12-12
ENG-44211-C: Extend canary gating to require 'no eviction' and 'stable eviction rate' in first 30 minutes before ramp (owner: SRE team lead - Marcos) - due 2025-11-30
ENG-44211-D: Add kernel fingerprinting telemetry and operator-level mismatch alerts for quant-converter binaries (owner: runtime-infra - Lin) - due 2025-12-07
ENG-44211-E: Expand regression harness to simulate KV cache pressure across sequence-length and concurrency distributions, run nightly (owner: QA - Emma) - due 2025-11-25
ENG-44211-F: Create preflight model-signature validator that checks expected memory reservation and opset compatibility before rollout (owner: model-onboarding - Kai) - due 2025-12-15
ENG-44211-G: Update autoscaler to honor backpressure signal from runtime when memory accounting deviates >10% (owner: autoscale - Jonas) - due 2025-12-05
ENG-44211-H: Post-deploy 'quant canary checklist' for PMs/engineers including exact traffic windows, failure thresholds, and rollback triggers (owner: Product - Maya) - due 2025-11-24
testing_and_validation: Reproducer created in internal harness: quant-eviction-repro-2025-11-09 (link: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/quant-eviction-repro-2025-11-09)
Nightly job added to run reproducer on multiple GPU types and with mixed sequence-length payloads
Manual runbook verification scheduled for next canary: validate eviction metrics stay <5/min for first 60 minutes
Canary will start at 02:00 UTC and ramp no faster than 5% every 15 minutes once metrics stable
observability_changes: New metric: quant_memory_accounting_mismatch{pool} -> tracks difference between expected and actual reservations
Trace spans instrumented for KV cache migration and eviction to correlate with OOM events
Add log scrubber rule to capture kernel signatures and quant-converter binary SHA during deployments
review_feedback: PM (Maya): emphasize preflight and canary checklist, require product sign-off for quant rollouts
SRE (Marcos): require autoscaler to surface backpressure instead of relying solely on memory headroom
Design (Amelie): add clearer operator UI elements showing eviction health for each pool
APPLIED: hotfix HWM and canary rollback; pending: autoscaler backpressure change
risks_and_open_questions: Risk: packed-weight memory assumptions may differ across GPU families - need wider hardware matrix coverage
Question: could other optimizations (fusion, prefetch) trigger similar accounting discrepancies? Need audit
Risk: extended canary requirements slow down model rollout velocity; balance with safeguards
Open: timeline for full KV cache reconciliation implementation may slip if other runtime priorities rise
postmortem_notes: Immediate rollback prevented a wider outage. The incident highlights a class of bugs where conversion/packing heuristics interact non-linearly with runtime reservation logic. We will treat quantized deploys as a new risk class and gate them with stronger canary controls and improved preflight checks. Revisit rollout runbook and shipping cadence for quant-enabled builds in Q1 2026.
